testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If your personal vehicle license is revoked or suspended, what happens to your CDL?

options.text: You can get a hardship license to drive a commercial vehicle.
You cannot get a hardship license to drive a commercial vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot get a hardship license to drive a commercial vehicle.
questions.explanation: If your personal vehicle license is revoked, canceled, or suspended, you cannot get a hardship license to drive a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: How should you do a parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it, bringing the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must stay completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: Compared to a full truck, an empty truck requires what stopping distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: A longer stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Empty trucks need longer stopping distances than full trucks because they have less traction.

questions.question: Is hanging meat as cargo stable or unstable?
questions.correctAnswerText: Unstable.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable because it swings during transport and has a high center of gravity.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.
Rely on what other drivers do to tell you if a train is coming.
Do not rely only on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Do not depend only on warning signals, gates, or flaggers. Be extra alert at crossings without gates or signals. Always assume a train could be coming at any railroad crossing.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air from the air brake system, what does this mean?

options.text: Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if tank pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic must check it.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to finish the trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Safely pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy, stop and get sleep. Driving while fatigued causes many fatal accidents.

questions.question: If your truck has ABS on only one axle, what happens when you brake?

options.text: You still have more control when braking.
It slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: You still have more control when braking.
questions.explanation: If your truck has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) on only one part, you still have more braking control than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: When should you slow down for a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down to a safe speed before entering a curve. Slowing down while in the curve could cause a skid.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection of the fifth wheel, what should you check?

options.text: Make sure the locking jaws are open.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Check that the fifth wheel locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin shaft, not around the kingpin head.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When stopped at a red light

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before each trip. If you have a trailer, make sure it is straight while you adjust your mirrors.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle before a trip, why should you look under it?

options.text: To see if the vehicle is on a slope.
To check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
To see if the vehicle is parked in a spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: Look under your vehicle for new leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like other vehicles, people, or low tree branches.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will need to:

options.text: Explain why you are checking each item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain why you are checking each item.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will inspect your vehicle and explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition with proper tread depth.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires in good condition with proper tread depth.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is more likely if your tire pressure is too low or your tire tread is worn. If you start to hydroplane, release the gas and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps your engine work properly:

options.text: Only when it is cold outside.
Both in cold and hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both in cold and hot weather.
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system. Antifreeze helps your engine even in hot weather, not just in cold weather.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks and the air brake system from too much pressure. It is usually set to open at 150 psi.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not have a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Do not need to know about crossings.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the proper way to cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: ABS brakes:

options.text: Stop your wheels from locking up.
Prevent your vehicle from going uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: If another driver is being aggressive, you should:

options.text: Ignore their hand gestures and stay calm.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore their hand gestures and stay calm.
questions.explanation: Do not let an aggressive driver provoke you. Avoid making eye contact and do not try to race them.

questions.question: A driver talking with passengers should be seen as:
questions.correctAnswerText: A distracted driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers who talk with passengers may not focus on the road. Be extra careful when driving near distracted drivers.

questions.question: Front wheel brakes work:
questions.correctAnswerText: In all conditions.
questions.explanation: Front wheel brakes work well in all road conditions. Front wheels are unlikely to skid, even on ice.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts means they are loose.

questions.question: To avoid being an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Plan ahead for realistic travel time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan ahead for realistic travel time.
questions.explanation: To avoid frustration that leads to aggressive driving, plan ahead and allow extra time for traffic delays. Drive at a safe speed, keep a safe distance from other cars, avoid making gestures at other drivers, and keep both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and check what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, have it checked right away.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of tire failure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Smoother steering
questions.explanation: Tire failure causes a loud bang, heavy thumping, or vibration. Heavy steering or fishtailing also signals tire problems. Stop to check your tires if you notice these signs.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, slow down to a safe speed.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, you should:

options.text: Not back in a straight line.
Not correct drift until you are far off course.
Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.
questions.explanation: Pull forward to reposition your vehicle whenever needed. Fix any drift right away by turning the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.

questions.question: Hydroplaning usually occurs:

options.text: Where water pools on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water pools on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water collects on the road. It can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water. Under-inflated tires or worn tread make hydroplaning more likely.

questions.question: After you change a tire, you should:

options.text: Stop soon to check that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop soon to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short time later to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.text: Push in the clutch when the engine is close to idle.
Release the clutch when the engine is close to idle.
Shift into neutral when the engine is close to idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the clutch when the engine is close to idle.
questions.explanation: When stopping, gradually apply brake pressure and stop smoothly. For a manual transmission vehicle, push in the clutch when the engine is close to idle.

questions.question: If you are driving very slowly and blocking other drivers, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers. This warns drivers behind you (if your local laws allow it).

questions.question: You are driving slowly in a construction zone and see a worker near the road. You should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down more.
questions.explanation: Always drive slowly in construction zones. Slow down even more if workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Your brakes fail while driving downhill. What is the best way to stop?

options.text: Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Use rumble strips to slow your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use an escape ramp.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, find an escape ramp quickly. If there is no escape ramp, drive into an open field or side road that is flat or goes uphill.

questions.question: Why do vehicles use multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions?

options.text: To make the vehicle run more smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: To provide extra gears.
questions.explanation: Many vehicles use multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions to provide extra gears.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, how many feet does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: Your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing. What happens?

options.text: You don't have to do anything about crossings.
The examiner may ask you to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
You must take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner may ask you to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: Water pooled on the road can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hydroplaning.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: How do you prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting to move?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in second gear.
Use the parking brake when you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To stop your vehicle from rolling backward when starting to move, partly engage the clutch before taking your foot off the brake pedal.

questions.question: Before a trip, check that:

options.text: The pedal grooves are not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal grooves are not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip check, make sure nothing blocks the pedals. Pedals should work well and have grooved surfaces for grip.

questions.question: Your horn should be used to:

options.text: Warn other drivers that you are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are near.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others of your presence. Only use it when needed because it can startle other drivers.

questions.question: Which vehicle requires a CDL?
questions.correctAnswerText: A school bus
questions.explanation: You do not need a CDL to drive military vehicles, emergency vehicles, farm equipment, or recreational vehicles. You also do not need a CDL for a straight truck carrying only your personal property that you are not selling. School buses require a CDL.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Tell the carrier about problems that need fixing
Make sure the vehicle is inspected regularly
Hold people responsible for inspecting the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the carrier about problems that need fixing
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report tells the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth for rear tires?
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Rear tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch of tread depth. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: While driving, what should you pay attention to?

options.text: Do not worry about what is on the sides of your vehicle
Watch what is happening on all sides of your vehicle
Do not worry about what is behind your vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch what is happening on all sides of your vehicle
questions.explanation: You must be aware of what is happening around your vehicle at all times. Look ahead at the road. Check your mirrors on both sides regularly while driving.

questions.question: What may you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?
questions.correctAnswerText: Check the engine oil level
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will need to check the engine oil level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: Which is not a type of distraction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Obtuse
questions.explanation: Distractions are physical (reaching for something), mental (talking with a passenger), or both (using a hand-held phone). Obtuse is not a type of distraction.

questions.question: If you have a fire in your vehicle and do not know how to put it out, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with water
Move away and wait for firefighters

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away and wait for firefighters
questions.explanation: If you do not know how to put out a fire, do not try. Move away from the flames and let firefighters handle it. This is especially important for fires involving hazardous materials.

questions.question: What happens to bridges in cold weather?

options.text: They have heaters to prevent freezing
They freeze before other road surfaces

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before other road surfaces
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Be extra careful on bridges when temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: How often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator in cold weather?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every day
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in an air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: What tread depth is needed in every major groove of a front tire?
questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Front tires need 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch of tread depth.
